## Binomial

<!-- TODO: Add the definition, explanation and intution of the binomial distribution, galton board figure perhaps? -->
Here there is the binomial distribution @eq-binomial 
$$
P(x|n) = {n \choose k} p^{x} \left(1 - p \right)^{n-x}
% \binom{n}{k}
$$ {#eq-binomial}

The generating moment function for the @eq-binomial-mgf distribution will be

$$
\begin{aligned}
M(t) &= \sum_{x}^{n} e^{xt} {n \choose k} p^{x} \left(1 - p \right)^{n-x} \\
&= \sum_{x}^{n} {n \choose k} \left(e^{t} p\right)^{x} \left(1 - p \right)^{n-x} \\
&= \left( (1-p) + e^{t} p \right)^n
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-binomial-mgf}




```{python}
#| label: fig-binomial-mgf
#| fig-cap: "Binomial probability mass function "

cm_color = mpl.colormaps['plasma']
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))

p_s = np.arange(0.2, 1, 0.2)
N_s = 10
nn = np.arange(N_s+1)

lbl_x = r"$p$"
lbl_y = r"p.m.f."
lbl_title_legend =r"$p_{i}$"
for p_s_i in p_s:
    # print(p_s_i)
    lbl_tmp = f"{p_s_i:0.1g}"
    pp = stats.binom.pmf(nn, N_s, p_s_i)
    ax.plot(nn, pp, label=lbl_tmp, color=cm_color(p_s_i), alpha=0.8)
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# ax.legend(title=lbl_title_legend)
ax.set(
    xlabel = lbl_x, ylabel = lbl_y
)

fig.legend(
    handles, labels, handlelength=0.75,
    bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.0), loc='upper center',
    ncols=5,
    frameon=False
    )

```

## Normal distribution

For the limit of $n \to \infty$ we get

TODO: add central limit theorem and a simple deduction

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lim_{n \to \infty} P(x|n) &= \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{n!}{(n-x)! x!}
p^{x} (1-p)^{n-x} \\
&\dots \\
&= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \sigma^2} } 
\exp\left( -\frac{ \left( x - \mu \right)^{2} }{2 \sigma^2} \right) 
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-normal-pdf}



## Poissonian distribution

TODO:Gaussian is not good for small values of $p$ 

Now, if before taking the number of attemps to infinity we take the probability of success $p \to 0$ and maning this change of variable $\lambda = n \times p$
 

$p(x, n) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \lim_{p \to 0} \frac{n(n-1)\dots(n-x+1)}{x! }  \frac{\lambda^{x}}{n^{x}} (1-\frac{\lambda}{n})^{n}(1-p)^{-x}$

$\lim_{n \to \infty} (1-\frac{\lambda}{n})^n = e^{-\lambda}$

we obtain a poisson distribution




$$ 
p(x, \lambda) = \frac{\lambda^{x}}{x!} e^{-\lambda}
$$ {#eq-poisson-pdf}

The @eq-poisson-pdf give us the probability of a rare event, with $p$ occurs $x$ times, where $\lambda$ is the mean value of $x$ 


## Geometric distribution

- Discrete memoryless property
First success in $n$ trials of Bernoulli events with probability $p$
$$
geometric = p (1-p)^{n-1}
$$ {#eq-geometric}
<!-- ## Multiple dimensions of binomial -->

the corresponding moment generation function (mgf) 

$$
M(t) = \frac{p}{e^{-t} - (1-p)}
$$ {#eq-geometric-mgf}




## Exponential distribution

- Exponential distribution describes the waiting time until the first event occurs in a Poisson distribution.
- Memoryless $P(T > t+s|T>s) = P(T>t)$
- The number of events in a time $\delta t$ has a poisson distribution.

lifetimes, radioactive elements decays

$$
P (T = t) = \lambda e^{-\lambda t}
$$ {#eq-exponential-pdf}




## Hazard Rate

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(T \le t+dt |T>t) &= 1 - P( T > t+dt |T>t ) \\
&= 1 - P( T > t+dt |T>t ) \text{Memoryless}\\
&= 1 - P(T>dt) \\
&= 1 - e^{-\lambda dt} \\
&\simeq \lambda dt 
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-hazard-rate}



## Gamma distribution

Waiting times for the $r$th arrival

$$
T_{r} = \omega_{1} + \omega_{2} + \ldots + \omega_{r}
$$

$$
T_{r} \sim \text{Gamma}(r, \lambda)
$$ {#eq-gamma-dist}

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(T_{r} > t) &= P(N_{t} \le r-1) \\
&= \sum_{k=0}^{r-1} \frac{e^{-\lambda t} (\lambda t)^k}{k!}
\end{aligned}
$$
